statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. The CME weekend halt ended near 22:00 UTC and Nasdaq-100 futures reopened in an orderly two-way band about 0.10% above Friday's settle, which resolves the reopening premium flagged in the prior assessment and returns tail to the low band, while stress remains high on the unresolved Strait of Hormuz disruption, elevated crude, a steepening long end and a sharply weaker August consumer read.
recommendation: Tail remains below the block threshold, so the deterministic mapping returns EA_ON for both NQ futures and NAS100 CFD. The Sunday restart window has now been observed and passed without dislocation, so the flagged observation window moves to the Monday U.S. cash open at 13:30-14:30 UTC, where the week's first opening auction concentrates liquidity and catalyst risk. Existing-position management and emergency protection logic are unaffected by this mapping.
headline: Nasdaq-100 futures reopen orderly about 0.10% above Friday's settle; tail eases back to the low band while stress stays high on Hormuz, crude and a steepening long end
body:
A live Nasdaq-100 price path exists again. CME Globex restarted near 22:00 UTC after the weekend halt, and the September Nasdaq-100 futures contract printed around 30,172.00, up roughly 30 points or 0.10% against Friday's 30,141.75 settle, inside an early band of about 30,167.75 to 30,198.75 on thin first-print volume. S&P 500 futures corroborate the tone at 7,810.25, up 0.07%, inside a seven-point 7,804.00 to 7,811.25 range at 22:16 UTC. The restart therefore produced a small two-way adjustment rather than a gap-and-go discontinuity.

That observation matters because the preceding assessment carried the highest conditional tail of its forecast into this hour specifically for the restart, on thin liquidity and two-sided weekend headline risk. The reopening has now been observed and shows no gap discontinuity, no one-way structure and no index holding near an extreme, so the reopening premium is removed rather than sustained. Tail returns to 13 and confidence improves to 74 because live price-path evidence, the main gap in the preceding hours, is available again.

The underlying stress backdrop is unchanged. The cash Nasdaq-100 closed Friday at 30,046.14, down 0.13% inside a 29,934.66 to 30,179.82 range and about 2.3% below its 30,762.20 52-week high. VIX finished at 14.25, down 2.60%, which keeps implied volatility subdued against the high stress reading. Treasury constant-maturity yields stood at 4.15% for the 2Y, 4.32% for the 5Y, 4.63% for the 10Y and 5.21% for the 30Y at the August 13 H.15 publication, with a 20-year sale due Wednesday into a steepening curve.

Friday's internals were split rather than one-way. Broadcom fell 5.94% while AMD rose 6.5% and Micron added 2.3%, and the shared delayed cross-asset feed shows technology down 0.46%, semiconductor equipment down 1.71%, software groups down more than 1% on the latest session and megacap direction mixed at two advancers against six decliners. That dispersion argues for uncertainty rather than persistent directional efficiency.

The macro backdrop softened materially into the weekend. The preliminary August University of Michigan sentiment index fell to 51.0 from 55.2, roughly an 8% decline against a consensus near 54.5, with expectations down 8.7% to 50.6 and year-ahead inflation expectations at 4.3%. July retail sales fell by the most in over a year. Those readings sit alongside financial conditions reported at their easiest since 1996, a combination that raises uncertainty about the Fed path without establishing a directional price mechanism.

The energy and geopolitical backdrop remains the dominant stress channel. WTI trades at $82.54, up 1.42% on the day and more than 5% on the week, with Brent at $88.76, while Strait of Hormuz transits stay far below the roughly 130 daily crossings recorded before the conflict. Iran's foreign minister continues talks with Oman on shipping routes while conditioning any reopening on Washington, and two ADNOC-owned tankers were struck by drones in the strait on August 13. The headline set stays genuinely two-sided rather than one-directional.

Tail therefore sits in the low band on observed evidence rather than on an absence of evidence. The next concentrated checkpoint is the Monday U.S. cash open at 13:30 UTC, where opening-auction continuation with shallow pullbacks would be the first genuine tail evidence of the new week; a narrow observation window is flagged there. The week adds known checkpoints rather than observed risk: Empire State and NAHB on Monday, housing starts, building permits and industrial production on Tuesday, the 20-year auction and July FOMC minutes on Wednesday, jobless claims, the Philadelphia Fed survey and Walmart on Thursday, and flash PMIs on Friday. Under the fixed mapping these inform stress and confidence until an actual price path is available to score.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding published Claude hours are available and uniformly green with EA_ON. Tail moved narrowly between 12 and 17, stress climbed from the high-60s into the low 80s through the European and U.S. weekend hours before easing back toward 72, and confidence ranged from 66 to 80. The entire window sits inside the cash-market weekend and the CME futures halt, so that trajectory reflects an accumulating energy, rates and consumer backdrop rather than any observed Nasdaq-100 price structure.
outlookSummary: With the restart observed and orderly, the forecast no longer carries a reopening premium. Tail eases to an overnight floor of 12 through the Asian hours, holds near 13 across the European session, and rises to a conditional peak of 17 across the Monday U.S. cash open at 13:30 UTC and the first full cash hour, where opening-auction continuation with shallow pullbacks would be the first genuine tail evidence of the new week. It then eases back toward 12-14 into the 20:00 UTC cash close and the post-close futures hours. Every forecast hour stays below the 20 threshold, so the mapping remains EA_ON throughout. Stress runs 68-70 overnight and peaks near 74 around the U.S. open, and confidence sits highest in the current hour at 74 because a live price path is available again, easing to 69 at the far end of the window.
